Ruefully

ROO-ful-ee · adverb

Hear It

What It Means

Ruefully is in a way that shows sorrow or regret, often with a wry or self-deprecating tone.

"I really should have read the instructions first," he said ruefully, staring at the pile of extra screws left over from the bookshelf.

Worked Example

Looking back at her overflowing closet, Elena admitted ruefully that she'd bought the exact same sweater in three different colors without noticing.

Ruefully describes tone -- a way of speaking or reacting that shows someone regrets something, often while half-laughing at their own mistake.

How Ruefully Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

regretfully

regretfully: in a manner that shows regret

remorsefully

remorsefully: in a way that shows deep regret for wrongdoing

Antonyms

proudly

proudly: in a way that shows satisfaction or self-approval

gleefully

gleefully: in a way that shows great delight

How Strong Is It? — apologetically → ruefully → despairingly

apologetically vs. ruefully

apologetically vs. ruefully: Saying 'sorry' apologetically is a simple, polite acknowledgment.

despairingly vs. ruefully

despairingly vs. ruefully: Reacting despairingly suggests a much deeper, hopeless sadness than a wry, rueful shrug.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — rue

root — rue: to feel regret about something (Old English hreowan)

suffix — -ful

suffix — -ful: full of (Old English)

suffix — -ly

suffix — -ly: in the manner of (Old English)

Put it together

Put it together: Ruefully comes from rue ("to regret") + -ful ("full of") + -ly ("in the manner of") -- literally "in a manner full of regret."
